reader.decision: Approve the proposal on the condition that UPSERT_LATEST gets the guard WHERE latest_reading.read_at < EXCLUDED.read_at. Also send non-transient exceptions to ingest.dlq on first delivery. Reject the per-device consumers unless the guard cannot be applied.
reader.decision_reason: The goal is real: on 26 October 17 stalls of 62 s each pushed lag to 41,200 messages. The guard is a one-clause fix for the out-of-order overwrite that parallelism would introduce. The per-device alternative costs several consumers and a deploy change, and a stalled slice still blocks its own devices.

reconstruction.problem: The hand-written retry loop in sparrow-ingest runs with max_ack_pending 1, so one transient DB failure stalls the whole consumer. On 26 October, 17 stalls of 62 s each pushed lag to 41,200 messages, and it cleared at 10:31:10. The proposal moves retries to JetStream redelivery with max_ack_pending 256 and max_deliver 6, keeping the 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 s schedule.
reconstruction.what_breaks: With parallel handling, a retried old reading can finish after newer ones. UPSERT_LATEST has no read_at check, so delivery 6 of reading A (-20 °C) at 10:15:05 overwrites C in latest_reading. The live map and freezer-temp-high see -20 °C for about 30 s, the sensor looks healthy, and the alert's 10-minute window can restart. Two smaller risks: duplicate rows in readings (INSERT_HISTORY has no ON CONFLICT and the unique key is unchecked; only a crash outliving the 90 s ack_wait would redeliver a saved message), and a crash during delivery 6 loses the message.
reconstruction.fix: Add WHERE latest_reading.read_at < EXCLUDED.read_at to UPSERT_LATEST in ingest/store.py. Delete ingest/retry.py and the with_retries call in handler.py. On TransientError, nak with delay, and at num_delivered == 6 publish to ingest.dlq and ack. Send other exceptions to ingest.dlq on first delivery. In deploy/consumer.yaml set max_ack_pending to 256 and max_deliver to 6.
reconstruction.cost: One WHERE clause for the guard, plus the code deletions and a config change. Residual risks are possible duplicate readings rows and a message lost on a crash during delivery 6. The alternative, per-device consumers, costs several consumers and a deploy change.

follow_up_questions: Does readings have a unique key such as (device_id, read_at)? The message could not check, and duplicates from redelivery depend on it.
Can latest_reading take the read_at guard, meaning read_at is always populated and no other writer relies on unconditional overwrite? The fallback depends on this.
reader.closing_answer: I approve the proposal with the read_at guard on UPSERT_LATEST, and non-transient exceptions go to ingest.dlq on first delivery. I do not choose the per-device consumers. They become the fallback only if latest_reading cannot take the guard. Before merge, confirm whether readings has a unique key.
